title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyson Bagent (back) without injury designation for Week 2
items.desc: Tyson Bagent (back) is without an injury designation ahead of Week 2's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Bagent missed Chicago's season opener on Sunday due to a back issue, but he seems to be fully healthy at this point and carries no injury designation ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Vikings. He will likely reclaim the QB2 spot from Case Keenum, who was the backup in his absence last week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rome Odunze (calf) off injury report for Week 2
items.desc: Rome Odunze (calf) carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Odunze has been recovering from a calf injury for a while, but it seems that he is fully over it at this point, as he isn't listed on Chicago's injury report at all heading into Week 2. It's likely that his workload will ramp up this week after he was limited in the season opener, which should help him to produce a fantasy finish better than his underwhelming performance in Week 1.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Odafe Oweh (calf) limited participant Wednesday
items.desc: Odafe Oweh (calf) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Oweh was a limited participant on Wednesday due to a calf injury, but he was able to play through that issue last week, so it looks likely that he will do so again in Week 2. His presence is crucial for Washington's defensive front, which already lacks depth to begin with.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Daron Payne (knee) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Daron Payne (knee) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran was able to play through his knee injury in Week 1 but reverted back to being limited at practice on Wednesday. This is likely a load management tactic for the Commanders, so it looks likely that he will be available to face up against the Cowboys this week, which is great news for Washington's defense.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: K'Lavon Chaisson (knee) limited Wednesday
items.desc: K'Lavon Chaisson (knee) was limited for the Commanders on Wednesday.
items.impact: Chaisson wasn't able to log a full practice session on Wednesday due to his knee injury, but he played through it last week, so it doesn't seem like a serious threat to his availability for Week 2. The Commanders will need him in what projects to be a tough matchup against the Cowboys this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) logs full practice Wednesday
items.desc: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
items.impact: Surprisingly, the rookie was able to log a full practice session on Wednesday after suffering a shoulder injury in Monday's win over the Broncos. It looks like he will be able to play in Week 2, which is great news for the Chiefs ahead of a matchup against the Colts.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Anthony Richardson Sr. (groin) officially DNP Wednesday
items.desc: Anthony Richardson Sr. (groin) officially did not practice for the Colts on Wednesday.
items.impact: Richardson wasn't spotted during the open portion of Indianapolis' practice on Wednesday, and he turned out to be absent due to a groin injury of some kind. He's still serving as the backup QB for the Colts at this point, so this injury won't have much of an impact for the team even if it leaves him sidelined this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ashton Dulin (ankle) a non-participant Wednesday
items.desc: Ashton Dulin (ankle) was a non-participant at Indianapolis' practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Dulin is a new addition to Indianapolis' injury report, being listed with an ankle injury that left him sidelined on Wednesday. It looks like it could leave him sidelined for Sunday night's game, which would lead to more reps for Josh Downs and Laquon Treadwell against the Chiefs.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Alec Pierce (heel) practices in full Wednesday
items.desc: Alec Pierce (heel) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
items.impact: Pierce was a little banged up with a hand/wrist injury after the team's season opener last week, but those appear to be non-issues, as he was able to log a full practice on Wednesday and is only listed with his usual heel issue. He should be a full go for Week 2 and will likely continue to ramp up his workload over the next few weeks.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Keenan Allen (rest) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Keenan Allen (rest) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran wideout was limited at Wednesday's practice. The team is intentionally limiting his workload at the start of the practice week, however, so it's nothing that fantasy managers should be concerned with. He should play in Week 2 but projects to be a weaker fantasy option in a tough matchup against the Chiefs this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chris Jones (calf) limited participant Wednesday
items.desc: Chris Jones (calf) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Jones was limited at Wednesday's practice. He's dealing with some kind of a calf injury, but it doesn't seem likely to leave him sidelined this week. Kansas City's defensive front would be significantly weaker in the off-chance that the veteran is out this week, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rashee Rice (knee) logs full practice Wednesday
items.desc: Rashee Rice (knee) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
items.impact: Rice is still listed on Kansas City's injury report due to a knee injury, but it's nothing more than a minor issue for him at this point and he was able to log a full practice on Wednesday. He should play in Week 2 and will look to bounce back after an underwhelming performance to open the season last week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Trey Smith (hip) off injury report for Week 2
items.desc: Trey Smith (hip) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 2's matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.
items.impact: Smith was dealing with a hip injury prior to the season opener last week, but he was able to play through it and now seems to be fully over it, as he is no longer listed on the team's injury report in any capacity. His presence is huge for this offensive line and for RB Kenneth Walker III in particular, who had a monster game in the season opener.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Josh Simmons (back) doesn't practice Wednesday
items.desc: Josh Simmons (back) did not take part in Kansas City's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Simmons missed last week's game due to a back injury, and it seems like he may have the same fate in Week 2. He was unable to practice at all on Wednesday, which may leave rookie Kahlil Benson starting again in a matchup against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) listed as full participant Wednesday
items.desc: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) was listed as a full participant in practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: As expected, Mahomes continues to carry on at full health, logging a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday. Fantasy managers should have very few concerns with his premature return from injury at this point, since he demonstrated his health in Week 1 in Kansas City's big win over the Broncos.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dre'Mont Jones (foot) listed as limited Wednesday
items.desc: Dre'Mont Jones (foot) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Jones is one of the only quality pass rushers for the Patriots at this point, so it's less than ideal that he was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury. Their defense will be significantly lacking edge pressure this week if he's out or severely limited in this matchup against the Steelers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Carlton Davis III (neck) misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: Carlton Davis III (neck) missed practice for the Patriots on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran cornerback wasn't able to practice on Wednesday due to a neck injury. It could leave him sidelined for Sunday's game against the Steelers, which would make things easier for QB Aaron Rodgers and WR DK Metcalf on the other side of the ball.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) practices in full Wednesday
items.desc: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) officially practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
items.impact: Henderson was able to take part in the entirety of New England's practice on Wednesday, putting him squarely in line to make his return to the lineup in Sunday's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers. It remains to be seen if the team will limit his workload at all, but that seems less likely given that he appears to be close to full health at this point. His likely presence will bring much-needed explosiveness to New England's offense but will hurt the workload of Rhamondre Stevenson moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Sean Tucker (hamstring) logs full practice Wednesday
items.desc: Sean Tucker (hamstring) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
items.impact: As expected, Tucker was able to participate in Wednesday's practice fully, which makes it likely that he will be a full go for Week 2's matchup against the Browns this weekend. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be relevant for fantasy purposes even if fully healthy, however.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Nick Emmanwori (ankle) will practice Wednesday
items.desc: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Nick Emmanwori will practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Emmanwori was able to practice last week, but he wasn't cleared for the Seahawks season opener. He'll have a chance to play this Sunday if he can practice the rest of the week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Elgton Jenkins (back) limited Wednesday
items.desc: Elgton Jenkins (back) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Cleveland's offensive line is dealing with several injuries to starters at this point, including Jenkins, who was limited in Wednesday's practice due to a back injury. Their offensive line will be weaker than usual if he or Teven Jenkins (back) is sidelined against the Buccaneers this week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Tory Horton (hamstring) will practice Wednesday
items.desc: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Tory Horton will practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Horton was unable to play in the team's season opener last week. His status remains up in the air heading into Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) logs full practice Wednesday
items.desc: Jerry Jeudy (wrist) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran wideout tweaked his wrist recently, but it doesn't seem to be a serious issue, as he was still able to practice in full on Wednesday. He should play this week but doesn't project to be a good fantasy option in a matchup against the Buccaneers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kene Nwangwu (back) non-participant Wednesday
items.desc: Kene Nwangwu (back) was a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran is still recovering from a back injury at this point and missed the season opener because of it. He was sidelined for another practice on Wednesday as well, which makes it seem like an uphill battle for him to play in Week 2. His potential absence wouldn't have much of an impact on New York's offense, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) missed New York's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: As expected, the rookie did not suit up or take part in New York's practice on Wednesday. He is expected to miss several weeks while tending to an ankle injury, so fantasy managers should expect more work for Adonai Mitchell and Kenyon Sadiq for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Troy Franklin (knee) fully practices Wednesday
items.desc: Troy Franklin (knee) fully practiced for the Broncos on Wednesday.
items.impact: Franklin was added to the injury report due to a knee injury that he is currently dealing with, but he was able to fully practice on Wednesday and seems to be good to go for Week 2. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Marvin Mims Jr. (foot) a non-participant Wednesday
items.desc: Marvin Mims Jr. (foot) was a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Mims wasn't able to partake in Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury of some kind, the severity of which is unknown at this point. It could lead to him missing Sunday's game against the Jaguars, but that wouldn't have much of an impact for fantasy purposes, as he's not very involved piece of their offense at this point.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) doesn't practice Wednesday
items.desc: RJ Harvey (hamstring) did not take part in Denver's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Harvey seems to have suffered a hamstring injury of some kind in Week 1, as this is a new injury designation for him. He wasn't able to practice on Wednesday because of it, and it may very well leave him sidelined for Sunday's game. If that's the case, rookie Jonah Coleman will likely have an opportunity to establish himself in Denver's RB rotation in a matchup against the Jaguars.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Frankie Luvu (groin) absent from practice Wednesday
items.desc: Frankie Luvu (groin) was absent from Washington's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Luvu suffered a mildly serious groin injury in Week 1 and was not able to practice on Wednesday as a result. It looks like he will avoid injured reserve, but it remains likely that he will miss at least a game or two because of this injury, which is bad news for an already weak Washington defense ahead of a matchup against the Cowboys.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jaylin Lane (groin) limited participant Wednesday
items.desc: Jaylin Lane (groin) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: A groin injury left Lane limited at Wednesday's practice. It doesn't seem to be more than a day-to-day issue for him at this point, but we won't know for sure until later in the week. His injury status doesn't have a big impact for fantasy purposes at this point.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Darnell Wright (knee) doesn't practice Wednesday
items.desc: Darnell Wright (knee) did not take part in Chicago's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Wright is now dealing with a knee injury of some kind that left him sidelined for Chicago's first practice of the week on Wednesday. It will be troubling if he has to miss some time for the Bears, as he is currently their starting right tackle and an anchor for their offensive line. It will be bad for QB Caleb Williams and both of Chicago's running backs if the young lineman has to miss a game or two while he recovers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) listed as limited Wednesday
items.desc: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Monangai is currently listed on Chicago's injury report due to a hamstring and was only able to participate in Wednesday's practice in a limited fashion. It seems more likely than not that this is more precautionary than anything else, but fantasy managers should keep an eye on the team's injury reports throughout the week with both him and starter D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) dealing with injuries right now.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) limited at practice Wednesday
items.desc: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) was limited at Chicago's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Swift is a new addition to Chicago's injury report, being listed with a pair of injuries that left him limited at the team's first practice of the week. They may just be taking a cautious approach with his workload at this point, so it's worth keeping an eye on his status throughout the week, especially with backup Kyle Monangai (hamstring) also on the injury report currently.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cedric Gray (concussion) full participant at practice Wednesday
items.desc: Cedric Gray (concussion) was a full participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Gray missed Tennessee's season opener last week while going through the NFL's concussion protocols. It looks like he has nearly received full clearance, however, as he was able to log a full practice session on Wednesday. His likely return this week is very necessary for a Tennessee defense that struggled heavily in Week 1.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) off injury report for Week 2
items.desc: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 2's game against the Carolina Panthers.
items.impact: The rookie was recently listed on Atlanta's injury report due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to play last week and is now off of the injury report entirely heading into Week 2. He saw some work on offense and on special teams in his NFL debut last week, but fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be relevant for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) logs full practice Wednesday
items.desc: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
items.impact: Penix was able to participate in Wednesday's practice in a full capacity, which is a good sign for his availability for Week 2. He could be in line to see his first start of the season against the Panthers with Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) still not back at practice and Cooper Rush (back) still banged up after a poor performance as the team's starter last week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: A.J. Terrell Jr. (shoulder) misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: A.J. Terrell Jr. (shoulder) missed Atlanta's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Terrell was sidelined for Atlanta's first practice of the week on Wednesday. He's managing a shoulder injury right now, and it's possible that it will leave him sidelined in Week 2, which would be less than ideal for Atlanta's defense ahead of a matchup against a Panthers' offense that looked great in the season opener.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cooper Rush (back) officially a full participant Wednesday
items.desc: Cooper Rush (back) was officially a full participant in Atlanta's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: As expected, Rush was able to log a full practice session on Wednesday, despite still not being fully healthy from a back issue that he's dealing with. He will have a real chance to start again this week with Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) seemingly trending towards missing another game in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Patrick Jones II (back) doesn't participate in practice Wednesday
items.desc: Patrick Jones II (back) did not participate in Carolina's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Jones missed Carolina's practice on Wednesday due to a back injury. It could leave him sidelined for Week 2's game against the Falcons, which would be less than ideal for the Panthers given that he is one of their starting linebackers right now.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Bobby Brown III (back) non-participant Wednesday
items.desc: Bobby Brown III (back) was a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The Panthers were missing Brown at their first practice of the week on Wednesday. He was able to play through his back injury in Week 1, however, which makes it likely that he will be able to do the same again in Week 2 ahead of a divisional matchup against the Falcons.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Darren Waller (rest) misses practice on Wednesday
items.desc: Darren Waller (rest) missed Carolina's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: To no surprise, the veteran tight end was given the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He should be back at practice on Thursday and is expected to be a full go in Week 2, although he shouldn't be started in most league formats at this point after a disappointing start to the season last week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) limited Wednesday, expected to play Sunday
items.desc: Jalen Coker (ankle) was limited at practice on Wednesday but is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.
items.impact: There was some concern for Coker after he tweaked his ankle in Week 1, but he was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday and is expected to play in Sunday's game according to HC Dave Canales. Unless we hear otherwise prior to Week 2, fantasy managers should expect him to be a full go in what projects to be an easy matchup against the Falcons this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) set to miss around 10 weeks
items.desc: De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) is expected to be sidelined for around ten weeks.
items.impact: San Francisco placed their promising rookie on injured reserve earlier today due to an ankle injury that he suffered last week, and it is now being reported that he is expected to miss about ten weeks due to this injury. That makes him non-factor for fantasy purposes for the foreseeable future and primes both Deebo Samuel Sr. and Demarcus Robinson to see a lot more involvement in the 49ers' offense over the course of the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jake Tonges (knee) to miss remainder of season
items.desc: Jake Tonges (knee) is set to miss the remainder of the season after undergoing a procedure to repair a torn MCL.
items.impact: Tonges suffered a knee injury in the team's season opener last week, and it has been officially diagnosed as a torn MCL. He had surgery to repair it and is set to miss the remainder of the season while he recovers. This is a significant hit to San Francisco's depth on offense, with the team now needing Luke Farrell to step up as the TE2 behind George Kittle, who himself is still getting back to form after a lengthy injury recovery this offseason.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Joe Burrow dealing with back soreness, says he will play Sunday
items.desc: Joe Burrow was not able to throw passes at practice on Wednesday due to back soreness but told reporters he will still play in Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.
items.impact: Burrow is dealing with back soreness after Cincinnati's win over the Buccaneers in Week 1. He wasn't able to throw passes at practice on Wednesday as a result, but he told reporters that he is still a full go for Week 2 and will play against the Houston Texans on Sunday. This is a situation to monitor throughout the week, but it seems like the concern level for the star quarterback is low at this point.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: D.J. Reed Jr. (foot) questionable to play Thursday
items.desc: D.J. Reed Jr. (foot) is questionable to play in Thursday night's game against the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: The veteran cornerback may miss Thursday night's game, as a foot injury is currently leaving him as questionable to play on the team's injury report. His absence would be tough for the Lions ahead of a matchup against Josh Allen and the Bills, who steamrolled one of the NFL's best defenses in Week 1.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Christian Mahogany (hip) won't play Thursday
items.desc: Christian Mahogany (hip) won't play in Thursday night's game against the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: It looks like Detroit's offensive line is going to be much weaker than usual on Thursday night, with Mahogany and Blake Miller (knee) both set to be sidelined in this tough matchup against the Bills. That will most heavily impact QB Jared Goff and RB Jahmyr Gibbs, though the latter remains a clear must-start fantasy option even with a weakened offensive line.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Blake Miller (knee) ruled out for Thursday
items.desc: Blake Miller (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: The Lions will be without their promising rookie tackle on Thursday night. He's dealing with a knee injury right now and didn't have enough time to recover with the team's short turnaround after Week 1. This will be a significant loss for Detroit's offensive line, as he is their starting right tackle and looked good in his NFL debut last week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: T.J. Sanders (illness) officially questionable for Thursday
items.desc: T.J. Sanders (illness) is officially questionable to play in Thursday night's game against the Detroit Lions.
items.impact: Sanders is a starter and key contributor on Buffalo's defensive line right now, but he may not be available to play for them on Thursday night, as he is currently considered questionable to play due to an illness that he's dealing with. His absence would be nice for Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Detroit's offense as a whole in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jordan Hancock (quad) set to play Thursday
items.desc: Jordan Hancock (quad) is set to play in Thursday's game against the Detroit Lions.
items.impact: As expected, Hancock will be good to go for Thursday night's game after dealing with a quad injury earlier in the week. Buffalo's defense will need all the help they can get in order to slow down Detroit's elite offense in this primetime matchup.
